text: Co-led a 53-member letter asking HHS and CMS to stop sharing Medicaid enrollee data with ICE. “The role of HHS should be to protect the health of all those living in this country and provide essential human services, not to be a watchdog for DHS or act as immigration enforcement”
quote: The role of HHS should be to protect the health of all those living in this country and provide essential human services, not to be a watchdog for DHS or act as immigration enforcement

text: Joined a letter to DHS and ICE after an oversight visit to the Dilley detention center, asking about DNA collection from detained families. “During our visit, we learned that ICE collects DNA samples from individuals detained at the facility, including parents and children.”
quote: During our visit, we learned that ICE collects DNA samples from individuals detained at the facility, including parents and children.

text: Voted against the Laken Riley Act (H.R. 29). It passed 264–159.

Led the California Democratic delegation in a letter urging CMS to reverse a deferral of federal funding for in-home care. “reverse a decision to defer $1.1 billion in federal funding for California’s In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) program”
quote: reverse a decision to defer $1.1 billion in federal funding for California’s In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) program

text: Voted against the Do No Harm in Medicaid Act (H.R. 498). It passed 215–201.
Voted against H.R. 1, the reconciliation bill the Clerk lists as the One Big Beautiful Act. It passed 215–214.

text: Warned that a SNAP administrative cost shift in H.R. 1 took effect October 1, 2026. “H.R. 1 cut the federal share of funding for SNAP administrative costs in half, meaning that states are now required to cover 75% of SNAP administrative costs.”
quote: H.R. 1 cut the federal share of funding for SNAP administrative costs in half, meaning that states are now required to cover 75% of SNAP administrative costs.

text: Introduced the Housing Tariff Exclusion Act to create a process to exclude some homebuilding materials from tariffs. “Families are already facing the high cost of buying or renting a home. We should not make it more expensive to build the homes our communities need,”
quote: Families are already facing the high cost of buying or renting a home. We should not make it more expensive to build the homes our communities need,

text: Announced a Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund provision for the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach in the House-passed Water Resources Development Act of 2026. “WRDA 2026 closes that loophole and requires the Army Corps to report annually to Congress on how the funding is distributed.”
quote: WRDA 2026 closes that loophole and requires the Army Corps to report annually to Congress on how the funding is distributed.

text: Voted against the Illegitimate Court Counteraction Act (H.R. 23). It passed 243–140.
Voted for H.Res. 352, calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism. It passed 421–1.
Voted against H.Res. 488, denouncing the antisemitic terrorist attack in Boulder, Colorado. It passed 280–113.
Voted for H.Res. 481, condemning the rise in ideologically motivated attacks on Jewish individuals in the United States. It passed 400–0.
